text.p: British retailer Kingfisher Plc said on Wednesday it believed its spread of businesses in expanding markets would help drive future growth.
Chief executive Sir Geoffrey Mulcahy told Reuters in an interview,"If you look to the future we believe we are well placed in growth markets."
Mulcahy declined to comment on speculation in the British press that Kingfisher might be looking at acquisitions, including stores put up for sale by Littlewoods.
"What we say is that we're very much focused on markets for the home and family....and the clear priority is to build our businesses in the UK and France and concentrate on doing just that," he said.
He said Kingfisher's B&Q and Darty were both market leaders in DIY and electricals respectively and that these were forecast to be relatively high growth markets.
Comet was a strong number two in the UK electricals market, where demand for home computers was expected to continue growing, he said.

Mulcahy said it was far too early to comment on sales in the current year. But when asked if uncertainty ahead of the general election had affected overall consumer demand he said consumers were already cautious about spending.
"I think consumers are cautious anyway," he said, "you have to offer them real value and real service and real choice if you're going to encourage them to spend money."

Improved operational efficiencies helped the group's performance last year. Mulcahy said B&Q made improvements in its supply chain and more than achieved a 20 million stg cost saving target identified a year ago.
Woolworths increased market share in toys, home essentials and home entertainment.
"I think Woolworths has demonstrated over the years that it is capable of continually improving the offer its makes to its customers," he said, "and achieving growth in the markets we've targeted."
He said chemist chain Superdrug was meeting its objectives in terms of the returns from stores which have been revamped.
Darty, the French electricals business, had done well in a difficult market. But Mulcahy said Kingfisher believed there were early signs that the market was improving.

Mulcahy said the group was getting to know French furnishing and electricals retailer BUT, in which it bought a 26 percent stake last year. The deal included a two year standstill agreement on Kingfisher increasing its stake.
Overall group gross margins were maintained last year, he added.
